rules.title: God Object candidate
rules.definition: A God Object candidate is a type that centralizes multiple unrelated responsibilities and exceeds multiple configured structural thresholds.
evidenceCriteria: The type exceeds at least the configured minimum number of structural signals.
Its declaration line count exceeds the configured line threshold.
Its method count exceeds the configured method threshold.
Its stored-property count exceeds the configured property threshold.
classificationGuidance: Require evidence of multiple responsibilities or multiple structural signals.
Do not classify a type as a God Object based on line count alone.
Distinguish a deliberately thin coordinator or facade from a type that owns unrelated business responsibilities.
severityGuidance: Use warning when the type exceeds multiple configured structural thresholds.
Increase severity only when broad coupling or unrelated responsibilities create a substantial maintenance risk.
refactoringGuardrails: Group properties and methods by responsibility.
Extract each responsibility into a dedicated type.
Keep only necessary coordination in the original type.

rules.title: Feature Envy candidate
rules.definition: A Feature Envy candidate is a method or computed property that depends more heavily on the data or behaviour of another type than on the type where it is declared.
evidenceCriteria: The declaration repeatedly reads properties or invokes methods belonging to another type.
The declaration uses little state or behaviour from its own containing type.
The externally accessed members form a cohesive operation that could reasonably belong to the other type.
classificationGuidance: Require concrete references to the envied type and its members.
Do not classify ordinary collaboration or a single delegated call as Feature Envy.
Consider whether moving the behaviour would improve cohesion without exposing private implementation details.
severityGuidance: Use warning when repeated external access clearly weakens cohesion.
Use info when the evidence is limited or the collaboration may be intentional.
refactoringGuardrails: Preserve ownership boundaries and existing behaviour.
Move behaviour only when the destination type can own it cohesively.
Avoid exposing additional mutable state solely to enable the move.

rules.title: Long Method candidate
rules.definition: A Long Method candidate is a function whose size and number of distinct responsibilities make its behaviour difficult to understand, test or change safely.
evidenceCriteria: The function exceeds the configured method line threshold.
The function contains several distinct phases or responsibilities.
Deep nesting, repeated conditionals or many local variables increase the effort required to follow its control flow.
classificationGuidance: Do not classify a function based only on its physical line count.
Require evidence that the function combines distinct operations or has difficult control flow.
Treat generated code, declarative data construction and straightforward mappings cautiously.
severityGuidance: Use warning when size and multiple responsibilities occur together.
Use info when the function is long but remains linear and cohesive.
refactoringGuardrails: Extract operations around meaningful responsibilities rather than arbitrary line ranges.
Preserve execution order, error handling and observable side effects.
Avoid creating small methods whose names do not clarify intent.
